title: Learningknight yclept Dixon
html_source:
A student called Dixon. The term “learningknight” may be Joyce’s own, but “yclept” was a Middle English term used up through the time of Geoffrey Chaucer, the sugar daddy of the English language.

yclept means ‘by the name of’. So, this means Learning Knight (medical student) by the name of Dixon.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Clepe
verb (used with object), cleped or clept (also ycleped or yclept ) cleping. Archaic.
to call; name (now chiefly in the past participle as ycleped or yclept).
